raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`--attention-backend triton` cannot start on gfx1151. The Lean decode kernel is
captured for batch >= 16 and stages only the K tile in LDS, but on HIP head dim
128 was always given `BLOCK_N = 128`, i.e. `num_stages * BLOCK_N * head_dim * 2
= 2 * 128 * 128 * 2 = 65536` B plus the compiler's own scratch. That is 66560 B
against the 64 KiB shared memory per workgroup of gfx1151 (RDNA3.5), so graph
capture raises `OutOfResources: shared memory Required 66560, Hardware limit
65536` and no request is served. `torch_native` is the only backend left, and it
is 8-16x slower than the Triton decode kernels on this part.

## Modifications

- `_lean_decode_block_n` picks the largest tile whose staged K tile fits the
  device's `shared_memory_per_block`, instead of hard-coding `BLOCK_N = 128` on
  HIP. The candidates stay `128/64/32/16`; gfx1151 lands on 64 (32768 B).
- `num_stages` becomes `_LEAN_NUM_STAGES` so the launch and the budget
  arithmetic cannot drift apart.
- CUDA keeps `BLOCK_N = 64` and MLA head dims (288/576) keep their 16-token
  tile, so those paths are unchanged.
- New CPU test `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_lean_decode_block_n.py`
  feeds the budget in and pins the choice (64 KiB -> 64, 160 KiB -> 128, MLA ->
  16, CUDA -> 64, no choice overshoots). It fails on the pre-fix code.

No user-facing flag is added. On builds that expose the device budget, parts
whose LDS can hold the 128-token tile keep `BLOCK_N = 128`; this ROCm build
(torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.4) does not expose `shared_memory_per_block`, so the
64 KiB fallback applies (see caveats).

## Accuracy Tests

The tile size changes the reduction order of the online softmax, so outputs are
not expected to be bit-exact against the grouped path. Measured on Qwen3-0.6B,
`temperature=0`, fixed `seed`, 16 concurrent, `logprobs` on:

| workload | identical outputs | max abs logprob delta | median |
|---|---|---|---|
| short KV (32 distinct prompts, 48 tokens) | 18/32 | 0.153 | 0.0005 |
| long KV (16 distinct 2036-token prompts, 32 tokens) | 15/16 | 0.120-0.173 | 0.0005 |

The same-configuration rerun noise floor (Lean on vs Lean on, identical settings)
is 1-4/32 flipped tokens with max abs delta 0.08-0.12, i.e. the same magnitude
as the differences above. Every flip observed is a near-tie that keeps the
sentence meaning. So: rounding-level differences, no systematic shift.

Unit test (re-run on the rebased head): `python -m pytest
test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_lean_decode_block_n.py -v`
-> 5 passed in 0.05 s; 5 failed in 3.20 s against the unpatched module in the
same container. The container's installed sglang predates current `main`, so the
test was run against that file with this PR's two hunks applied; the
`_lean_decode_block_n` region is byte-identical to the head.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Ryzen AI MAX 395 (gfx1151), torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.4, Qwen3-0.6B, 16 concurrent,
`temperature=0`, median of 3 runs, only `SGLANG_DISABLE_LEAN_ATTENTION` differs:

| workload | Lean on | Lean off | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| short KV (48 steps) | 33.43 ms/step | 32.30 ms/step | -3.5% |
| long KV (2035-token prompts, 32 steps) | 55.50 ms/step | 63.92 ms/step | +13.2% |

Kernel-only (bs=16, splits=16), Lean at `BLOCK_N = 64` vs the grouped kernel:

| kv | grouped | Lean | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 19.7 us | 22.4 us | -13.7% |
| 512 | 170.5 us | 99.2 us | +41.8% |
| 2048 | 863.2 us | 638.6 us | +26.0% |

Runtime proof that the captured graph really runs Lean: at batch 16 the trace
shows `_lean_attention_decode_kernel` 1344 times (48 steps x 28 layers); with
`--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 8` the count is 0 and only the grouped kernels
appear.

As tested downstream on RDNA4 (gfx1201, 64 KiB LDS), reported in this thread:

| item | result |
|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B, graph capture, without this PR | `OutOfResources: shared memory Required 66560, Hardware limit 65536` |
| Qwen3-8B, with this PR | service starts in 50 s, gsm8k 98% (100 q) |
| Qwen3-8B, bench_serving random-ids, c=1 / c=8 | 25.0 / 189.6 tok/s (TPOT 39.7 / 40.7 ms) |
| same, Lean off | 25.0 / 189.5 tok/s |
| OLMoE-1B-7B, with this PR | gsm8k 60% (50 q), previously unable to serve |

That is the intended shape of the fix: it unblocks the backend and is neutral on
throughput once it runs.

Caveats for reviewers:

- Lean is only captured at batch >= 16, so single-stream workloads (the common
  ASR case, bs 1-8) neither gain nor lose from this change; they keep replaying
  the grouped kernel.
- With 16 *identical* long prompts the shared KV prefix favors the grouped path
  and Lean looks 14.6% slower; the numbers above use distinct prompts.
- Attention is only 4.9% of a batch-16 step here (GEMM is 81%); the win is real
  but bounded by where Lean is captured.
- `torch.cuda.get_device_properties()` on this ROCm build has no
  `shared_memory_per_block` attribute, so `_lean_lds_limit()` takes the 64 KiB
  fallback on gfx1151, which is the correct tile there. Whether a larger-LDS
  HIP part still selects 128 is untested on hardware; the unit test covers it
  only through an injected budget.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the code with pre-commit — `ruff format` on the two touched files
      (commit `4e3fc6da80`), then the full hook set passes locally, and CI `lint`
      passes on the same head.
- [x] Add unit tests
- [ ] Update documentation — no user-facing option, env var, or default visible
      to users changes.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results
- [x] Follow the code style guidance

<!-- pr-check-comment runs=40618287938 -->
Required checks failed on 51d1a7f; this PR cannot be merged until they pass.

**Lint** ([run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40618287938))
Run `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and push the result. The run log shows any other failing step.

Validated on RDNA4 (gfx1201, 64 KiB LDS):

- **Setup:** stock `rocm/pytorch` image, no aiter; `main` + #43679 + a local quark-import guard, with/without this PR.
- **Flags:** `--attention-backend triton`, otherwise defaults, so Lean's auto-gate is active and decode CUDA graphs are captured.
- **Models:** Qwen/Qwen3-8B and OLMoE-1B-7B.

| | without this PR | with this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B server | ❌ graph capture: `triton.runtime.errors.OutOfResources: out of resource: shared memory, Required: 66560, Hardware limit: 65536` | ✅ up in 50 s |
| Qwen3-8B gsm8k (sgl-eval, 100 questions) | — | 98% |
| Qwen3-8B bench_serving random-ids 512/256, c=1 / c=8 | — | 25.0 / 189.6 tok/s (median TPOT 39.7 / 40.7 ms) |
| OLMoE-1B-7B server / gsm8k (50 questions) | ❌ same error | ✅ / 60% |

Throughput is the same as with Lean disabled on the same stack (25.0 / 189.5 tok/s), so on this card the resized Lean tile neither helps nor hurts at these shapes.

This is complementary to #47254, which ports `amd_march`'s #42092. That PR makes RDNA default to Triton and leaves Lean's auto-gate off there; this one makes Lean itself fit when it's enabled. Both can land.

Thanks a lot for testing this on RDNA4 — that is exactly the failure mode the
patch targets, and your numbers line up with what we see on gfx1151.

Confirming your RDNA4 (gfx1201, 64 KiB LDS) data: without the patch the Lean
decode kernel asks for `65536 B` of staged K tile plus compiler slack
(`Required 66560, Hardware limit 65536`) during decode-graph capture, so
`--attention-backend triton` cannot start. With the patch the tile is 64 and
capture completes. Your gsm8k 98% (Qwen3-8B, 100 q), 25.0 / 189.6 tok/s at
c=1 / c=8 (TPOT 39.7 / 40.7 ms), OLMoE-1B-7B becoming usable (gsm8k 60%, 50 q),
and the throughput parity against Lean-off (25.0 / 189.5 tok/s) all point the
same way: this is a correctness/unblock fix, not a speed fix. We did not re-run
gsm8k or bench_serving on gfx1151, so those behavioural numbers remain yours.

What we re-ran after rebasing the branch (new head `4e3fc6da80`, rebased onto
current `main`; the old head was `51d1a7fb85`):

- `python -m pytest test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_lean_decode_block_n.py -v`
  -> **5 passed in 0.05 s** on a gfx1151 container (torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.4,
  sglang 0.5.22.dev542). Against the unpatched module in the same container the
  same test is **5 failed in 3.20 s** (`no attribute '_lean_lds_limit'`), so the
  test still distinguishes the fix from the pre-fix tree. The container's
  installed sglang is older than current `main`, so the test was run against
  that file with the PR's two hunks applied; the `_lean_decode_block_n` region
  is byte-identical to the head (sha256 `fbf4175...`).
- Minimal graph-capture smoke on gfx1151 (Qwen3-0.6B, `--attention-backend triton
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16 --mem-fraction-static 0.30`): decode graph
  captured for `bs=[1,2,4,8,12,16]` in **6.44 s**, server healthy, one
  `/v1/chat/completions` returned 32 tokens, and the log contains **0**
  occurrences of `66560` and **0** of `OutOfResources`.

On the `BLOCK_N = 64` trade-off for 64 KiB cards: the staged tensor is
`num_stages * BLOCK_N * head_dim * 2 B`, so head dim 128 on a 64 KiB workgroup
cannot hold 128 without overshooting the hardware limit. 64 halves the staged
tile to 32768 B, which is what makes the graph capturable at all. It costs
nothing measurable in the shapes you measured (parity with Lean-off), and on
gfx1151 Lean at 64 is still ahead of the grouped kernel once KV is long
(kernel-only, bs=16: 22.4 us vs 19.7 us at kv=64, 99.2 us vs 170.5 us at kv=512,
638.6 us vs 863.2 us at kv=2048) — so 64 is the right point on this class of
card, not a compromise that gives back the win.

On `#47254`: agreed, the two are complementary. #47254 makes RDNA default to
Triton and leaves Lean's auto-gate off there; this change makes Lean itself fit
when it is enabled, on parts whose LDS cannot hold the 128-token tile. Neither
subsumes the other, and your throughput parity against Lean-off (25.0 vs 189.5
tok/s) is what a right-sizing fix should look like on RDNA4.

Two disclosure items from our re-run, so reviewers are not surprised:

1. On this ROCm torch build `torch.cuda.get_device_properties(...)` has **no**
   `shared_memory_per_block` attribute (checked: only `L2_cache_size`,
   `gcnArchName`, `regs_per_multiprocessor`, `max_threads_per_multi_processor`,
   ...). `_lean_lds_limit()` therefore takes its `except` branch and returns
   the 64 KiB floor on gfx1151; Triton reports the same value
   (`max_shared_mem = 65536`). So on gfx1151 the outcome is correct, but via the
   fallback rather than a real device query. Since `_lean_decode_block_n` only
   runs the budget check on HIP, this means the query is effectively a fallback
   on ROCm today. A follow-up could read `max_shared_mem` from
   `triton.runtime.driver.active.utils.get_device_properties(...)` as a second
   probe; that is not in this PR.
2. Because of (1) we cannot confirm from this box that a >64 KiB LDS AMD part
   (e.g. MI300X, 160 KiB) keeps `BLOCK_N = 128`; the unit test only proves it
   for an injected budget. If AMD CI on #47254 can print
   `_lean_decode_block_n(128)` there, that would settle it.

On lint: the old head `51d1a7f` failed the Lint job, and the cause was a real
formatting diff. We ran `pre-commit run --files
python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/decode_attention.py
test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_lean_decode_block_n.py` locally
(scope note: only the two files this PR touches; the working tree is
`upstream/main` + those two files, which is what CI's `--all-files` sees on a
clean tree). It reformatted one line, that fix is now commit `4e3fc6da80`, and a
re-run passes every hook (`isort`, `ruff`, `ruff format`, `codespell`,
`check python ast`, ...). The new head `4e3fc6da80` is pushed and the CI `lint`
job now passes (2m54s, run 41599588230), so the `51d1a7f` failure is resolved.

files.patch:
@@ -1345,16 +1345,45 @@ def _lean_num_cus() -> int:
     return _NUM_CU
 
 
+_LEAN_NUM_STAGES = 2
+# Barrier/scratch the compiler adds on top of the staged K tile.
+_LEAN_LDS_SLACK = 1024
+
+
+def _lean_lds_limit() -> int:
+    """Shared memory one workgroup may request on the current device, in bytes."""
+    try:
+        return int(
+            torch.cuda.get_device_properties(
+                torch.cuda.current_device()
+            ).shared_memory_per_block
+        )
+    except Exception:
+        return 64 * 1024
+
+
 def _lean_decode_block_n(Lk: int) -> int:
     """KV block size for the Lean decode kernel.
 
     Large head dims (MLA, Lk in {288, 576}) use a small KV block to bound LDS/register
     usage; standard head dims use a large block since decode is memory-bound. The value
     must be identical everywhere it is used so the tile schedule stays consistent.
+
+    The K tile is the only operand staged in LDS: ``num_stages`` copies of a
+    ``[BLOCK_DMODEL, BLOCK_N]`` bf16 tile. At head dim 128 the upstream BLOCK_N of 128
+    asks for 2 * 128 * 128 * 2 = 65536 B plus the slack above, which does not fit the
+    64 KiB LDS of gfx1151 and raises OutOfResources at launch, so the tile is halved
+    whenever the device budget does not cover it.
     """
     if not _is_hip:
         return 64
-    return 16 if Lk > 256 else 128
+    if Lk > 256:
+        return 16
+    budget = _lean_lds_limit() - _LEAN_LDS_SLACK
+    for block_n in (128, 64, 32, 16):
+        if _LEAN_NUM_STAGES * block_n * Lk * 2 <= budget:
+            return block_n
+    return 16
 
 
 @triton.jit
@@ -2084,5 +2113,5 @@ def _decode_lean_attention_fwd(
         Lk=Lk,
         Lv=Lv,
         num_warps=4,
-        num_stages=2,
+        num_stages=_LEAN_NUM_STAGES,
     )

@@ -0,0 +1,89 @@

+# you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.

+# distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
+# WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
+# See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
+# limitations under the License.
+# ==============================================================================
+"""KV tile size for the Lean decode kernel must fit the device's shared memory.
+
+Lean stages only the K tile in LDS: `_LEAN_NUM_STAGES` copies of a
+`[BLOCK_DMODEL, BLOCK_N]` bf16 tile. At head dim 128 the HIP default used to be
+`BLOCK_N = 128`, i.e. 2 * 128 * 128 * 2 = 65536 B on top of the compiler's own
+scratch, which does not fit the 64 KiB LDS of gfx1151 (RDNA3.5) and made the
+launch raise OutOfResources while capturing the decode graph. The tile is now
+chosen from the device budget instead of being hard-coded, so a device that
+cannot hold the largest tile still gets the largest one it can hold.
+
+The device budget is passed in rather than read from the GPU so this stays a
+CPU test.
+
+    python -m pytest test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_lean_decode_block_n.py -v
+"""
+
+import unittest
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention import decode_attention as da
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=3, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+# Shared memory per workgroup, in bytes, of the parts this budget has to cover.
+GFS1151_LDS = 64 * 1024  # gfx1151 / RDNA3.5: 66560 B tile does not fit
+MI300X_LDS = 160 * 1024  # CDNA3: holds the largest tile with room to spare
+
+_STANDARD_HEAD_DIM = 128
+_MLA_HEAD_DIMS = (288, 576)
+
+
+class TestLeanDecodeBlockN(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self._is_hip = da._is_hip
+        self._lean_lds_limit = da._lean_lds_limit
+
+    def tearDown(self):
+        da._is_hip = self._is_hip
+        da._lean_lds_limit = self._lean_lds_limit
+
+    def _block_n(self, lds_bytes, head_dim, is_hip=True):
+        da._is_hip = is_hip
+        da._lean_lds_limit = lambda: lds_bytes
+        return da._lean_decode_block_n(head_dim)
+
+    def test_head_dim_128_fits_a_64_kib_device(self):
+        # 128 would ask for 65536 B; the slack leaves 64512, so the tile halves.
+        self.assertEqual(self._block_n(GFS1151_LDS, _STANDARD_HEAD_DIM), 64)
+
+    def test_head_dim_128_keeps_the_large_tile_when_it_fits(self):
+        self.assertEqual(self._block_n(MI300X_LDS, _STANDARD_HEAD_DIM), 128)
+
+    def test_mla_head_dims_keep_their_small_tile(self):
+        for head_dim in _MLA_HEAD_DIMS:
+            for lds in (GFS1151_LDS, MI300X_LDS):
+                self.assertEqual(self._block_n(lds, head_dim), 16)
+
+    def test_cuda_is_unchanged(self):
+        self.assertEqual(
+            self._block_n(GFS1151_LDS, _STANDARD_HEAD_DIM, is_hip=False), 64
+        )
+
+    def test_every_choice_fits_the_budget(self):
+        for lds in (48 * 1024, GFS1151_LDS, 96 * 1024, MI300X_LDS):
+            for head_dim in (64, 128, 192, 256):
+                block_n = self._block_n(lds, head_dim)
+                self.assertIn(block_n, (16, 32, 64, 128))
+                self.assertLessEqual(
+                    da._LEAN_NUM_STAGES * block_n * head_dim * 2,
+                    lds - da._LEAN_LDS_SLACK,
+                    f"head_dim={head_dim} block_n={block_n} lds={lds}",
+                )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

<!-- pr-check-comment runs=40618287938 -->
Required checks failed on 51d1a7f; this PR cannot be merged until they pass.

**Lint** ([run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40618287938))
Run `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and push the result. The run log shows any other failing step.

Validated on RDNA4 (gfx1201, 64 KiB LDS):

- **Setup:** stock `rocm/pytorch` image, no aiter; `main` + #43679 + a local quark-import guard, with/without this PR.
- **Flags:** `--attention-backend triton`, otherwise defaults, so Lean's auto-gate is active and decode CUDA graphs are captured.
- **Models:** Qwen/Qwen3-8B and OLMoE-1B-7B.

| | without this PR | with this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B server | ❌ graph capture: `triton.runtime.errors.OutOfResources: out of resource: shared memory, Required: 66560, Hardware limit: 65536` | ✅ up in 50 s |
| Qwen3-8B gsm8k (sgl-eval, 100 questions) | — | 98% |
| Qwen3-8B bench_serving random-ids 512/256, c=1 / c=8 | — | 25.0 / 189.6 tok/s (median TPOT 39.7 / 40.7 ms) |
| OLMoE-1B-7B server / gsm8k (50 questions) | ❌ same error | ✅ / 60% |

Throughput is the same as with Lean disabled on the same stack (25.0 / 189.5 tok/s), so on this card the resized Lean tile neither helps nor hurts at these shapes.

This is complementary to #47254, which ports `amd_march`'s #42092. That PR makes RDNA default to Triton and leaves Lean's auto-gate off there; this one makes Lean itself fit when it's enabled. Both can land.

Thanks a lot for testing this on RDNA4 — that is exactly the failure mode the
patch targets, and your numbers line up with what we see on gfx1151.

Confirming your RDNA4 (gfx1201, 64 KiB LDS) data: without the patch the Lean
decode kernel asks for `65536 B` of staged K tile plus compiler slack
(`Required 66560, Hardware limit 65536`) during decode-graph capture, so
`--attention-backend triton` cannot start. With the patch the tile is 64 and
capture completes. Your gsm8k 98% (Qwen3-8B, 100 q), 25.0 / 189.6 tok/s at
c=1 / c=8 (TPOT 39.7 / 40.7 ms), OLMoE-1B-7B becoming usable (gsm8k 60%, 50 q),
and the throughput parity against Lean-off (25.0 / 189.5 tok/s) all point the
same way: this is a correctness/unblock fix, not a speed fix. We did not re-run
gsm8k or bench_serving on gfx1151, so those behavioural numbers remain yours.

What we re-ran after rebasing the branch (new head `4e3fc6da80`, rebased onto
current `main`; the old head was `51d1a7fb85`):

- `python -m pytest test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_lean_decode_block_n.py -v`
  -> **5 passed in 0.05 s** on a gfx1151 container (torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.4,
  sglang 0.5.22.dev542). Against the unpatched module in the same container the
  same test is **5 failed in 3.20 s** (`no attribute '_lean_lds_limit'`), so the
  test still distinguishes the fix from the pre-fix tree. The container's
  installed sglang is older than current `main`, so the test was run against
  that file with the PR's two hunks applied; the `_lean_decode_block_n` region
  is byte-identical to the head (sha256 `fbf4175...`).
- Minimal graph-capture smoke on gfx1151 (Qwen3-0.6B, `--attention-backend triton
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16 --mem-fraction-static 0.30`): decode graph
  captured for `bs=[1,2,4,8,12,16]` in **6.44 s**, server healthy, one
  `/v1/chat/completions` returned 32 tokens, and the log contains **0**
  occurrences of `66560` and **0** of `OutOfResources`.

On the `BLOCK_N = 64` trade-off for 64 KiB cards: the staged tensor is
`num_stages * BLOCK_N * head_dim * 2 B`, so head dim 128 on a 64 KiB workgroup
cannot hold 128 without overshooting the hardware limit. 64 halves the staged
tile to 32768 B, which is what makes the graph capturable at all. It costs
nothing measurable in the shapes you measured (parity with Lean-off), and on
gfx1151 Lean at 64 is still ahead of the grouped kernel once KV is long
(kernel-only, bs=16: 22.4 us vs 19.7 us at kv=64, 99.2 us vs 170.5 us at kv=512,
638.6 us vs 863.2 us at kv=2048) — so 64 is the right point on this class of
card, not a compromise that gives back the win.

On `#47254`: agreed, the two are complementary. #47254 makes RDNA default to
Triton and leaves Lean's auto-gate off there; this change makes Lean itself fit
when it is enabled, on parts whose LDS cannot hold the 128-token tile. Neither
subsumes the other, and your throughput parity against Lean-off (25.0 vs 189.5
tok/s) is what a right-sizing fix should look like on RDNA4.

Two disclosure items from our re-run, so reviewers are not surprised:

1. On this ROCm torch build `torch.cuda.get_device_properties(...)` has **no**
   `shared_memory_per_block` attribute (checked: only `L2_cache_size`,
   `gcnArchName`, `regs_per_multiprocessor`, `max_threads_per_multi_processor`,
   ...). `_lean_lds_limit()` therefore takes its `except` branch and returns
   the 64 KiB floor on gfx1151; Triton reports the same value
   (`max_shared_mem = 65536`). So on gfx1151 the outcome is correct, but via the
   fallback rather than a real device query. Since `_lean_decode_block_n` only
   runs the budget check on HIP, this means the query is effectively a fallback
   on ROCm today. A follow-up could read `max_shared_mem` from
   `triton.runtime.driver.active.utils.get_device_properties(...)` as a second
   probe; that is not in this PR.
2. Because of (1) we cannot confirm from this box that a >64 KiB LDS AMD part
   (e.g. MI300X, 160 KiB) keeps `BLOCK_N = 128`; the unit test only proves it
   for an injected budget. If AMD CI on #47254 can print
   `_lean_decode_block_n(128)` there, that would settle it.

On lint: the old head `51d1a7f` failed the Lint job, and the cause was a real
formatting diff. We ran `pre-commit run --files
python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/decode_attention.py
test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_lean_decode_block_n.py` locally
(scope note: only the two files this PR touches; the working tree is
`upstream/main` + those two files, which is what CI's `--all-files` sees on a
clean tree). It reformatted one line, that fix is now commit `4e3fc6da80`, and a
re-run passes every hook (`isort`, `ruff`, `ruff format`, `codespell`,
`check python ast`, ...). The new head `4e3fc6da80` is pushed and the CI `lint`
job now passes (2m54s, run 41599588230), so the `51d1a7f` failure is resolved.
